newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares reverse early losses, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares reverse early losses, close higher.

text.p: Greek shares chalked up mild gains on Thursday, reversing early session losses to settle 0.31 percent higher in high turnover. Banks, industrials and small-caps climbed higher but construction shares stumbled.
"It was Alpha Credit Bank and Hellenic Sugar which closed limit up that led stocks higher. It looks like we'll stay in the 900-930 range a while longer," said a floor trader at a state brokerage.

Financial press reports that the government is planning to tax interest earned on T-bills, derivatives such as swaps, options and FRAs and revamp the tax status of mutual funds, finds the market cautious as players await the 1997 budget.
The finance ministry cut 40 basis point cut in the marker 12-month T-bill, down to 12.30 percent. The issue came to market on Thursday.
Greece's current account deficit in the first half widened 47 percent to $3.15 billion on lower tourism and EU receipts as the trade deficit was stable.

"This is bad news but not as bad as it appears at first sight because it was caused by a deterioration in tourism due to bad weather. The combined effect from the fall in tourism and EU funds was a 10.6 percent drop in total invisible receipts," said ING Barings.
The Athens general share index closed up 0.31 percent, or 2.83 points higher at 928.64 from Wednesday's 928.64 close after opening at 924.64 points.
Turnover rose to 10.3 billion drachmas from 8.79 billion on Wednesday on volume of 6.19 million shares, boosted by a block trades in Keranis and Aspis Pronia.

The market was mixed as losers led gainers 115 to 93 with 22 issues unchanged on 230 traded. Banks gained 0.42 percent, industrials moved 0.50 percent higher but construction gave up 0.42 percent. Small-caps firmed 0.17 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas closed at 584-602. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, gained five drachmas to close at 4,205.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $10.14-$11.14. The strike price is set at $99.6 and the warrants expire October 8 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 3,901-4,147 drachmas at the close. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
